clue.text: A game swimmer sounding cheerful

parts.note: whist is a card game for four players
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A sporty fish seems to be in a cheerful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who whistles a tune is usually in good spirits, so the activity conveys a happy mood.

clue.text: Not in favour of the soil being churned up

indicators.note: soil that is churned up is turned over and mixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone objects to the earth being dug over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned up' rearranges the seven letters of THE SOIL; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hostile to a proposal is to oppose it, to be set against it.

clue.text: Good man bearing with anger to no avail

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword's stock good man
E, east, is a compass bearing
to rile is to anger or irritate

explanation.surface: A saintly man puts up with wrath, but it achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces; 'anger' is a verb here, giving RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile efforts are fruitless, producing no result, which is what doing something to no avail means.

clue.text: 23 people from Belgium

definitions.meaning: refers to the answer at 23 across, loyal supporters
read cryptically as men of Liège, a city in Belgium

explanation.definitionFit: Liegemen were vassals bound to serve a lord faithfully, so they are devoted followers; split, the word suggests natives of the Belgian city.

clue.text: Sound fellow, though quite a spouter!

indicators.note: the clue's first word tells us to listen to how the next word is pronounced

parts.note: a geezer is British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A man of good character, though he talks a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound fellow' pretends to be a reliable chap; 'Sound' instead signals a homophone. A geyser is a hot spring that shoots up water, hence a spouter.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser periodically spouts jets of hot water and steam from the ground.

clue.text: This might well be set in code in parts

indicators.note: the phrase says these letters could be reworked into something else, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A message might be divided up when written in cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might well be' rearranges the nine letters of SET IN CODE; 'This' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sectioned has been cut or divided into separate segments.

clue.text: The sultan getting fresh food in

parts.note: a salad is a dish of fresh raw vegetables

explanation.surface: A ruler is brought some fresh greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century Muslim sultan of Egypt and Syria who opposed the Crusaders.

clue.text: One court document in about ten is redrafted

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, between the two parts of the outer

parts.note: re is Latin for 'about' or 'concerning'
ten is given as written
a writ is a written order issued by a court

explanation.surface: One legal paper in roughly ten gets revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' and 'is' are only links; 'in' places the court paper between the two parts of 'about ten'.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been redrafted has been written again in a new version.

clue.text: Raise tax in the Spanish quarters just the same

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'

indicators.note: the tax is placed within the surrounding letters

parts.note: E, east, is a quarter of the compass, taken twice since both quarters are the same
VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax

explanation.surface: Increase duty on Spanish districts all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts Britain's value added tax inside; 'quarters just the same' means the same compass point twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift something up to a higher position.

clue.text: Profited from ringing a woman taken in

indicators.note: one word encircles another, as a ring surrounds a finger

parts.note: to have used something is to have profited from it
her is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone gained by phoning a woman who was admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like a phone call but means surrounding the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest who is ushered is shown or escorted inside.

clue.text: It's fine-like the crossword!

definitions.meaning: weather that is ... is settled and good
a crossword is set by its compiler, and is ideally fair to solvers

explanation.definitionFit: A barometer reading of settled weather describes a fine spell; a clued puzzle should be both composed and just.

clue.text: Coach-building industry

definitions.meaning: industry here means hard work and application

explanation.surface: A firm that builds coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence names an old European stagecoach and also steady, careful effort.

clue.text: Having a brush about the time to hold gold

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the inner one between them

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a date is a particular time
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone with a hairbrush turns up around the hour, carrying gold.
explanation.walkthrough: A brush is a fox's tail, so 'Having a brush' means tailed. 'about' is circa, abbreviated; 'to hold' puts the chemical symbol for gold inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Caudate means possessing a tail, and a fox's tail is called its brush.

clue.text: He's fired with enthusiasm to distress others

definitions.text: He's fired with enthusiasm to distress others

parts.words: He's fired with enthusiasm to distress others
parts.note: reads as a keen person, but 'fired' means setting things alight, and the distress is caused by a blaze

explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist deliberately starts fires that harm other people and their property.

clue.text: Remove obstruction found in a river

indicators.note: the obstruction sits within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the England-Wales border
a let is an old word for hindrance, kept in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Clear away a blockage discovered in a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete text is to strike it out or erase it.

clue.text: Sporting note a union's got

parts.note: D is a note of the musical scale
an alliance is a union of parties

explanation.surface: A sporty musical note belongs to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' means flirtatious play, not athletics; 'got' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is idle amorous play, and to sport with someone is to trifle or flirt.

clue.text: Men expect her work to suit them very well

definitions.text: Men expect her work to suit them very well

parts.words: Men expect her work to suit them very well
parts.note: a woman whose job is fitting garments, so her work should 'suit' clients literally

explanation.definitionFit: A tailoress is a woman who makes and fits suits and other clothes.

clue.text: Done any working out for relief?

indicators.note: the letters are worked out into a new order

explanation.surface: Has anyone finished exercising to relax?
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkiller, something taken to ease pain.

clue.text: The author of "Love Isn't Free"

indicators.note: letters set free from their order may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A book title naming its writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' is the anagram signal on LOVE ISN'T; 'of' links to the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of fiction books is an author.

clue.text: A looker round

parts.note: something that looks and is round, rather than a person who peers about

explanation.definitionFit: The eyeball is the spherical organ of sight.

clue.text: Exceptional child likely to achieve success

parts.note: odd means unusual or out of the ordinary
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: An unusual boy is probably going to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite at short betting odds is expected to win, so it is the probable victor.

clue.text: Stop being a passenger!

parts.note: sounds like urging someone to pull their weight, but means getting off a railway carriage

explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to alight from a train at the end of a journey.

clue.text: The end result of striking approach

parts.note: workers out are on strike
to come is to approach

explanation.surface: The final consequence of industrial action closing in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' is industrial action, OUT on strike; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or final result of events.

clue.text: No set-back splits heel and true supporter

indicators.note: the inner letters split the outer word into two parts

parts.note: a ship that heels over is said to list
O, a zero, stands for no or nothing

indicators.note: the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to lay is to set down

explanation.surface: No setback divides a scoundrel from a faithful ally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like a cad but means to lean over, as a ship does; 'back' reverses the synonym for 'set'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist stays faithful to a cause or ruler, so is a steadfast backer.

clue.text: Craft shown about appropriate wagers

indicators.note: the craft is placed around the other word

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a craft
to appropriate is to take

explanation.surface: A trade's skill is displayed, with suitable bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown' is only a link; 'appropriate' is a verb, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes are sums of money bet on an outcome.

clue.text: Europeans getting their heads together causes talk!

definitions.text: Europeans getting their heads together causes talk!

parts.words: Europeans getting their heads together causes talk!
parts.note: French people literally putting heads together, the French word for head being doubled up

explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people, literally head to head in French.

clue.text: Dreadful rat able to make good in Canada

indicators.note: letters made dreadful are scrambled out of their order

explanation.surface: A nasty rat manages to make good in a far country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges RAT ABLE; 'to make good' is padding linking to the place in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is a western province of that North American country.

clue.text: Sanctimonious knave or beastly fighting man?

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
a cad is a dishonourable man, a knave

explanation.surface: A holier-than-thou rogue, or a brutal fighter?
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is a horseman in a bullfight who goads the bull with a lance, so he fights a beast.

clue.text: Blue steel possibly required by an engineer

parts.note: CE stands for civil engineer

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An engineer needs blue steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges 'steel', placed after the engineer; 'required by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeste is a sky-blue colour, from the French for heavenly.

clue.text: Condemns pieces of writing

definitions.meaning: a judge passes judgement on, or punishes, a convict

explanation.definitionFit: A judge sentences a convict to punishment, and sentences are also units of prose.
